chapters.title: Chapter 985. I Can’t Wait To See The Look Of Her Reaction! (Gonna Be Peak)
paragraphs: The night had descended upon the estate like a heavy shroud, swallowing the jagged edges of the mountains in darkness. Rex moved through the corridors not like a guest, but like a shadow reclaiming its territory.

His boots were silent on the marble as he approached Aurelia’s private wing. He had expected the familiar: the scent of expensive lavender, the soft glow of candlelight against silk sheets, and the intimate confines of a bedchamber.
But as he pushed open the heavy oak doors to her inner sanctum, he found himself standing in something else entirely.
It wasn’t a bedroom. It was a vast, dimly lit drawing room that felt more like a fortress than a place of rest.
High vaulted ceilings disappeared into darkness, and the only light came from a dying fire in a massive hearth, casting long, dancing shadows across the walls.

There was no bed in sight, only leather armchairs, towering bookshelves, and a single, expansive velvet sofa that sat like a throne in the center of the room. The space felt exposed, stripped of the comforts of femininity, as if Aurelia had excised anything soft from her life.
"You’re late."
The voice came from the darkness ahead. Rex turned to see a door at the far end of the room creak open.

Aurelia stepped into the firelight. She had changed out of her training leathers into something darker, a robe of deep crimson silk that clung to her frame like spilled wine, but her face remained unchanged, stern, pale, and etched with a resolve that made her look older than her years.
"I made sure I wouldn’t be disturbed," she said, her eyes tracking his movement with the precision of a hawk. "You’re finally here."
Rex didn’t apologize. He simply crossed the room, his eyes scanning the strange, barren opulence of her private space.
"You live like a soldier in a siege, Aurelia... Where is the comfort?"
"Comfort is a luxury for those who believe they are safe," she replied coldly.
She gestured toward the velvet sofa. "Sit."
Rex obeyed, sinking into the plush cushions. The fire crackled between them, sending sparks upward like dying stars.

As he watched her settle into the opposite end of the sofa, a dark, poisonous satisfaction began to coil in his gut. His mind wasn’t filled with the tenderness one might expect from a man visiting a woman at her most vulnerable hour.
No, his thoughts were venomous.
’She thinks she wants connection,’ he thought, a cruel smirk threatening to break his composed mask. ’She thinks she wants someone to share the burden...’
’She has no idea that I am here to make sure she carries it until it crushes her spine...’

He knew Theo was right. He had seen the truth in the boy’s terrified eyes, the truth about the rot festering at the heart of their lineage, the truth about what Aurelia had sacrificed and what she had become to maintain control.
Tonight, he wasn’t here to comfort her. He was here to dismantle her.
He would peel back her layers of denial until she was standing naked before the horror of her own choices.
But he would play the part first. He would be the steady hand she craved before he became the blade that cut her open.
"You look like you’re still carrying the weight of the world on those shoulders," Rex said quietly, breaking the silence.
His voice was smooth, deliberately lowering the tension just enough to draw her in. "Even now, after tonight’s... demonstration."
Aurelia leaned back, her head resting against the velvet, though her body remained coiled. "The weight doesn’t leave just because you’ve had a good fight, Rex.
"It just becomes easier to breathe around it." She turned her head to look at him, her gaze searching. "Why did you really come? Was it just to fulfill a command?"
Rex leaned forward, elbows resting on his knees, invading the space between them. The firelight caught the predatory glint in his eyes.
"I came because you asked me to speak plainly. And I am a man who finds immense pleasure in being honest."
"Honesty is rare in this house," she murmured, her voice softening despite herself. "Most people here speak in riddles and threats wrapped in courtesy."

"Then let’s set aside the courtesy," Rex said, his tone shifting, becoming something darker, more intimate. "Tell me, Aurelia, when you close your eyes at night in this empty fortress you’ve built, do you actually believe you’re protecting them?"
"Or do you know you’re just guarding a tomb?"
Aurelia flinched as if he had struck her. The question was too pointed, too close to the raw nerve of her guilt.
"That is a dangerous question to ask a woman in my position."
"Danger is the only thing that makes us feel alive, isn’t it?" Rex countered, watching her reaction with hungry interest. "You spent the evening trying to break a training post."
"But we both know you weren’t trying to break the wood... You were trying to break the lie."

Rex let out a low, rumbling laugh that vibrated through the expensive cushions of the sofa. It wasn’t a sound of amusement; it was a sound of genuine, mocking delight at the trap he had already sprung.
He watched her carefully, noting the way her jaw tightened at his implication.
"You want honesty, Aurelia?"
"Fine... Let’s talk about honesty." His smile vanished as quickly as it had appeared, replaced by a cold, analytical stare. "Let’s talk about your precious Theo."
"Let’s talk about the trail of wreckage he’s left behind while you were busy playing the stoic matriarch..."
"The failed negotiations, the broken alliances, the debts—actually, tangibly, debts that his incompetence has piled up like corpses in a ditch."
Aurelia stiffened, her fingers digging into the crimson silk of her robe.
"Theo made mistakes," she said, though her voice lacked its usual conviction. "He is young, and he is impulsive."
"He is a liability," Rex interrupted sharply. "And every liability has a price."
"Right now, the price of his survival, the price of keeping this household from being torn apart by the vultures circling outside these walls, rests squarely on your shoulders."
"Because you are the one who allowed him to become this."
Aurelia closed her eyes. The accusation cut deeper than any blade she had encountered in the training hall.
"I know," she whispered, the admission tasting like ash. "I know I failed him..."
"I failed to guide him, to contain him." She opened her eyes, looking at Rex with a desperate, almost sacrificial resolve. "What do you want from me, Rex?
"Name it. If there is a way to repay the damage he has caused, if there is a price I can pay to secure his future and this family’s stability..."
"I will pay it. I will do whatever is necessary."
Rex leaned back, swirling the dark liquid in his coffee cup. The firelight played across his features, making him look like something ancient and predatory.
"Whatever is necessary?" he repeated, tasting the words. "That’s a dangerous promise to make to a man like me."
He took a slow sip of the bitter coffee, letting the silence stretch between them until it became unbearable. Aurelia watched him, her heart hammering against her ribs.

"So, let’s make the terms explicit, then," Rex said casually, as if he were discussing the weather. "For the next three days... the three days it will take me to finish reorganizing and training this pathetic excuse for a household next week."
"You... are going to be having sex with me."
The silence that followed was absolute. Even the fire seemed to freeze mid-crackle.
Aurelia froze, her mouth parting slightly. "Wh... what? H-huh? What?"
The words stumbled out of her in a rush of pure disorientation. "What are you talking about?"
Rex took another leisurely sip of his coffee, watching her over the rim of the cup with unblinking eyes.
"Wait, what do you mean!?" Aurelia suddenly demanded, her voice rising in pitch, cracking with shock and rising fury. "What on earth are you talking about, Rex?"
"That is preposterous! That is--"
Rex let out another bark of laughter, this one louder and more cruel. "Oh? You haven’t heard the rumors?"
He set the cup down on the low table with a decisive clink. "You’ve been so busy ruling this house that you’ve forgotten how the real world operates."
"You think everything runs on gold and signed treaties?"
He leaned closer, his shadow engulfing her. "Every debt that comes to me, Aurelia... every favor, every concession, every piece of broken territory that needs mending... I don’t accept coin."
"Gold is transactional; it’s impersonal... I prefer something more... intimate."
Aurelia shook her head, her mind racing to reject the insanity of it. "You... you can’t be serious."
"I am deadly serious," Rex purred, his eyes darkening. "Take Iris, for example."
"Do you remember her desperation? Her grief over that dead boyfriend of hers?"
"Well... let’s say I helped her. I gave her the closure she begged for."
"But I didn’t ask for money." His voice dropped to a conspiratorial whisper. "I fucked her senseless until she was carrying my child."
"That was the price for her peace... That was the payment for her debt."

chapters.title: Chapter 986. Just The Reaction I Liked To See When I was Tremor!
paragraphs: Aurelia felt the blood drain from her face. The memory of Iris, the hollowed-out, haunted look in the girl’s eyes weeks prior, flashed through her mind.
She had thought it was grief. She had thought the girl was simply mourning.
But now, looking at the cold calculation in Rex’s expression, the truth settled in her gut like molten lead.
The horror of it began to dawn on her. Theo’s mistakes weren’t just political blunders; they were debts owed to a monster.
And Rex wasn’t here to help her fix them; he was here to collect.
The realization hit her with the force of a physical blow: Theo was telling the truth.
Everything the boy warned her about—every terrifying implication of Rex’s true nature—was real. And now, she had just volunteered to pay the bill.

The blood rushed to Aurelia’s face, not with shame but with a volcanic, white-hot rage that threatened to consume her entire being. Her hands trembled against the velvet cushions, her nails digging so deep into the fabric that the sound of tearing silk punctuated her breathing.
"You absolute... depraved animal," she spat, the words dripping with venom.
Her voice wasn’t loud, but it carried the lethal edge of a blade. "I knew you were ruthless..."
"I knew you were manipulative. But this? This level of shamelessness is beyond anything I imagined."
She stood up abruptly, the crimson silk of her robe swirling around her ankles like blood. "You have no dignity, Rex... None at all!"
"You’ve turned this household into your personal hunting ground..."
"You fuck Diana in the west wing while the servants pass by her door, and you fuck Iris in the servants’ quarters without the slightest concern that someone might hear her screams!"
"You don’t care about honor, you don’t care about propriety; you simply take what you want because you know no one has the spine to stop you."
Rex didn’t flinch. Instead, he leaned back further, crossing one leg over the other with infuriating nonchalance.
"Propriety is the cage that weak men build to feel safe from men like me, Aurelia..."
"Why should I pretend to care about the opinions of people who are already beneath me?"
"Because there are standards!" she screamed, her composure finally shattering. "There are boundaries that separate a man from a monster!"
Rex’s lips curled into a smile that didn’t reach his cold, dead eyes. "Oh, you think you know my history here?"

"You think you understand the depth of my... appetites within these walls?" He paused, letting the firelight catch the cruel amusement dancing in his pupils. "You talk about shame as if it were something I’ve ever possessed."
"Even your mother, Elaris... she was the first one I claimed in this very house. And she enjoyed every moment of the surrender."
The world seemed to stop. For a heartbeat, there was no sound, no crackle of fire, no distant wind.
Then, something inside Aurelia snapped. The mention of her mother, a woman she had revered, a woman who had been a symbol of grace and authority, was the final desecration.
"You bastard!" she shrieked.
Her body moved before her mind could process the impulse. She launched herself across the space between them, her fist cocked back, fueled by decades of pent-up fury and the raw wound of his insult.
It was a punch aimed to shatter bone, a strike meant to crack that smug, arrogant skull open.
But she never connected.
Halfway through the arc of her swing, Aurelia felt an invisible wall slam into her fist. Her knuckles stopped millimeters from Rex’s nose, frozen in midair as if pressed against solid diamond.
She grunted with effort, muscles straining until they burned, her shoulder joint screaming under the unnatural pressure, but her arm would not budge.
Then, the horror deepened.
"What--" The word died in her throat.
A cold, crushing sensation wrapped around her torso like iron bands. She tried to recoil, to stumble backward, but her legs refused to respond.

Her entire body became rigid, locked in place by an unseen force that felt like it was holding every individual muscle fiber hostage. She was suspended in mid-motion, a statue of rage and terror, unable to move even an inch.
Rex hadn’t even stood up. He remained seated, one hand still casually resting on his knee, while his other hand hovered slightly off the armrest.
A faint, violet distortion in the air, the telltale sign of his telekinetic grip, shimmered around her.
"Don’t exhaust yourself, Aurelia," Rex said quietly, his voice terrifyingly calm. "Anger is a wasteful emotion when you have no power to back it up."
Aurelia’s eyes bulged as she stared at him, her breath coming in shallow, panicked gasps. The helplessness was absolute.
She was a prisoner in her own skin, caught between the man who had insulted her bloodline and the invisible power that now commanded her body.
"You... you monster," she choked out, though the words felt weak against the overwhelming pressure crushing her lungs.
"Monster is such a subjective term," Rex replied, rising slowly from the sofa.

He walked toward her until he was inches away, his breath warm against her frozen cheek. "I prefer ’collector. ’And tonight, Aurelia, I’ve come to collect on a debt that has been overdue for far too long."

Rex leaned in closer, his face inches from hers, his eyes reflecting the dying embers of the fire like twin pits of hellfire. The telekinetic grip tightened just enough to make her ribs ache, a reminder of how easily he could snap her spine if he so desired.
"You know," Rex whispered, his voice carrying a cruel intimacy that made her skin crawl, "your son was right about me."
"All along, little Theo saw the truth... He saw the predator beneath the suit, the wolf beneath the skin."
"He tried to warn you, but you were too busy playing queen to notice the kingdom was already rotting from the inside out."
Aurelia’s eyes burned with unshed tears of fury. "Theo is a child who sees shadows where there are none--"
"No," Rex cut her off, his smile widening. "Theo sees exactly what I am."
Then, the air around him began to vibrate with a different kind of energy. It wasn’t the invisible pressure of telekinesis, but something heavier, more primal.
The ground beneath them groaned. Dust motes began to swirl violently around Rex’s face as chunks of stone and debris rose from the floorboards, drawn to him by an irresistible force.
Aurelia watched in paralyzed horror as his Earthen Authority manifested. The stones didn’t just float; they fused, grinding together with a sound like breaking bones.

Dark, jagged granite swirled around his features, forming a grotesque, unmoving visage. When the dust settled, Rex’s face was gone, replaced by Tremor’s mask, a terrifying, ancient visage of cracked stone with glowing runes that pulsed like veins of magma.
He no longer looked human; he looked like an avatar of destruction itself.
The sight shattered what remained of Aurelia’s composure. The terror broke through the anger, unleashing a torrent of grief and accusation that she had held back for years.
"You think this frightens me?" she screamed, though her voice wavered with the sheer impossibility of what she was seeing. "You think this mask makes you a god?"
"All it does is confirm what everyone has whispered behind closed doors!"
"You didn’t just come here to collect debts, Rex... you came here to destroy everything we built!"
Her words came faster now, each one a desperate attempt to wound him. "You destroyed Aethelgard."
"You tore through our alliances like they were tissue paper..."
"You sowed chaos in our territories just to watch the fires burn from your balcony."
"You’ve bled this land dry, leaving nothing but ashes and broken promises in your wake!"
She choked on a sob of pure rage. "My grandmother... she warned us."
"Long before you arrived, she saw the darkness in the wind..."
"She accused you of being a plague, a walking catastrophe that would devour everything beautiful."
"She said you had no soul, only hunger. And God help me, she was right."
Rex, behind the stone mask, didn’t move. He didn’t flinch at her accusations.
He simply stood there, the glowing runes on the granite face pulsing in time with her heartbeat.
"It’s too late now, isn’t it?" Aurelia continued, her voice cracking as she realized the futility of her words. "The damage is done... and the blood is spilled."
"You’ve dismantled our legacy piece by piece, and you’re standing here laughing while you do it."
"You don’t want power, Rex... You don’t even want money."
"You just want to satisfy your own twisted desires... You want to see us crawl, and you... want to see us break."
She stared into the empty eye sockets of the stone mask, her own eyes wet with tears. "You do whatever you want, simply because you can."
"Because you enjoy watching the light go out in people’s eyes."
"You’re not a man, Rex... You’re just... a void."
A silence fell over the room, heavier than the stone mask itself. The fire had burned down to glowing coals, casting a sickly orange light across the scene.
Rex stepped forward, the stone mask grinding softly as he moved. The sheer presence of his power made the very air feel thick and unbreathable.
"A void?" Rex’s voice came through the mask, distorted and echoing as if spoken from the bottom of a canyon. "Perhaps."
"But even a void has needs, Aurelia... And tonight, I find myself very, very hungry."

chapters.title: Chapter 987. A Wise Choice Indeed To Protect Aethelgard Using Her Body**
paragraphs: The raw agony of helplessness burned in Aurelia’s chest, more painful than any physical wound. Her defiance, however, refused to die.
Even as her body remained suspended in his invisible grip, her eyes blazed with a hatred so pure it seemed to challenge the very darkness of the room.
"I would rather rip my own heart out with my bare hands," she hissed through clenched teeth, each word a struggle against the pressure on her lungs, "than submit to a monster like you."
"I would choose death... I would choose the sweet release of the grave before I let your filthy hands touch me."
"Kill me now, Rex... End this farce and save me from the humiliation."
Rex’s head tilted to the side, the stone features of Tremor’s Mask catching the dim light.
"Death?" he mused, the distorted voice echoing unnaturally. "Death is too quick, Aurelia."
"Death is an escape. And I have never been fond of letting people escape their obligations."
Suddenly, the invisible pressure changed. It was no longer just holding her in place; it began to contract.

Aurelia’s eyes flew wide as she felt the telekinetic force tighten around her limbs, her ribs, and her throat. It wasn’t a sudden snap but a slow, methodical constriction, like a python tightening its coils around prey.

The pain began as a dull ache in her joints, then sharpened into a searing agony that radiated through every nerve ending. She felt her bones creak under the impossible pressure, the sensation of her own body betraying her as it was crushed inward.
"You think you have leverage because you have pride," Rex said, his voice cold and detached as he watched her suffer. "But pride is worthless when you’re breaking apart."
Aurelia let out a strangled cry, her body convulsing in the air.
The pain was an overwhelming white-hot tide that drowned out all thought. Her vision began to blur at the edges, dark spots dancing before her eyes.
"And don’t worry about the consequences," Rex continued, stepping closer until the stone mask was all she could see. "Don’t worry about Aethelgard."
"Don’t worry about the household as well... If you choose to die, and if you choose to resist until you break, I will simply burn it all."
"I will slaughter every servant, every guard, every child who shares your blood."
"I will reduce Aethelgard to a wasteland of ash and bone before the sun rises."
"I have nothing to lose, Aurelia. I started with nothing, and I will leave with nothing."

A scream tore from Aurelia’s throat a raw, primal sound of pure torment. She fought against the crushing force, her muscles straining to the point of tearing, but it was like fighting the ocean itself.
The pain reached a crescendo, a crescendo that felt as though her very soul was being squeezed out of her body.
"Please," she gasped, the word broken by another spasm of agony. "Stop... please..."
The defiance finally shattered. The weight of her responsibility, the faces of the people she protected, and the legacy she carried collided with the unbearable torment Rex was inflicting.
She couldn’t let them die. She couldn’t let his cruelty erase everything she had fought to preserve.
"I yield!" she shrieked, the words punctuated by a sob of absolute defeat. "I yield! Stop it! Please, just stop!"
The crushing pressure vanished instantly. Aurelia collapsed, but she didn’t hit the floor.
Rex caught her mid-fall with his telekinesis, lowering her gently onto the velvet sofa.
She lay there gasping, her body shaking with violent tremors, her breath coming in ragged, sobbing gulps. The pain was still fresh in her mind, a phantom agony that made her want to writhe.
Then, she felt it. A sudden, overwhelming surge of warmth.
A brilliant, golden light emanated from Rex’s outstretched hand. Supreme Healing.

The magical energy washed over her like warm honey, seeping into her bruised muscles, knitting together the microscopic tears in her flesh, and soothing the screaming nerves. Within seconds, the agony retreated, leaving behind only a profound, hollow exhaustion.
Rex pulled his hand back, the stone mask dissolving back into his human features. His expression was calm, almost serene, as if he hadn’t just tortured a woman to the brink of death.
"There," he said softly, watching her regain her composure. "Pain is a temporary distraction."
"I prefer you at your best."
Aurelia looked up at him, her eyes red-rimmed and hollow. The fire in them had gone out, replaced by something far more terrifying: resignation.
"Why?" she whispered, her voice hoarse. "Why go through that?"
Rex leaned over her, his fingers tracing the line of her jaw with terrifying gentleness. "Because I wanted you to understand the stakes, Aurelia."
"This isn’t a negotiation. This is a choice." He leaned closer, his breath ghosting over her lips. "Choose wisely."
"If you give yourself to me, if you accept the terms, Aethelgard lives... Your people live. Your precious Theo lives."
"But if you refuse..." His smile returned, cold and promising ruin. "Then you can die knowing you were the one who killed them all."
The silence that followed Rex’s ultimatum was heavier than the stone mask he had worn moments before. Aurelia lay on the crimson sofa, her chest rising and falling in rapid, shallow jerks.

The Supreme Healing had mended her bones and soothed her muscles, but it could not heal the violation of her spirit. Her body felt terrifyingly pristine, warm and supple, as if the torture had never happened, and that was the most insulting part of all.
Her mind was a battlefield. One part of her screamed to run, to flee into the night and never look back, to choose her own dignity over the survival of a kingdom that had already failed her.
But another part—the part that had been forged in the fires of leadership and tempered by years of responsibility—was stronger.
’I cannot let them die,’ she told herself, the words repeating like a grim mantra in the hollow chambers of her mind. ’Not because of what he is, but because of what they are.’
’Theo. The servants. The children are playing in the courtyard.’
’The thousands who sleep soundly believing Aethelgard is safe.’
’I am terrified,’ she admitted to herself in a moment of raw honesty that no one would ever see. ’I am terrified of his touch, terrified of his cruelty, terrified of what this will make me.’
’But I will protect them. I will swallow my pride like poison if it means they live to see tomorrow.’
"I understand," she said finally.

Her voice was flat, stripped of all emotion, the sound of someone who had already died inside and was now simply inhabiting a corpse. She forced herself to sit up, the silk robe slipping slightly off one shoulder.
"I accept your terms... Three days... The household remains untouched."
"Aethelgard remains whole."
Rex’s eyes gleamed with something predatory and satisfied. "A wise choice, Aurelia. Truly."
He moved closer, the heat from his body rolling off him in waves. When his hand came to rest on her thigh, Aurelia flinched involuntarily, a small gasp escaping her lips.
The contact was electric, sending a shiver of pure revulsion through her nerves, yet her body betrayed by the very healing magic he had used reacted with a traitorous hum of arousal.
"Don’t fight it," Rex whispered against the shell of her ear. "Your mind may hate me, but your body knows exactly what it wants."
He leaned down, his lips finding the sensitive column of her throat. Aurelia closed her eyes tight, squeezing them shut until she saw stars, trying to retreat into the fortress of her own mind.
But Rex was relentless. His mouth was hot, his tongue tracing the pulse point that hammered erratically beneath her skin.
"Nnh... ahh..." A broken sound escaped her.
She wanted it to be a sob, but it came out as something softer, something more dangerous. Her hips jerked involuntarily as his teeth grazed her collarbone.
"There it is," Rex purred against her skin. "That’s the sound of surrender."
He pulled away just enough to look her in the eyes, his gaze dark with hunger. With one fluid motion, he pushed her back against the cushions.
The sound of her silk robe rustling against the velvet was loud in the quiet room—shhh shhh—as he began to undo the sash.
"This is for the debt, Aurelia," he murmured. "And this is for the pleasure."
As his hands moved over her, exploring the curves he had already claimed in his mind, Aurelia felt the first wave of genuine arousal crash over her, a shameful, involuntary response to his dominance.
When his mouth descended to her breast, her back arched off the sofa.
"Ah! H-hah... no... please..." Her protests were weak, crumbling under the onslaught of sensation. "Mmmph... ahh!"

The room filled with the sounds of their collision: the wet sounds of kisses, the ragged breathing that filled the space between them, and the rhythmic thump-thump of Rex’s body pressing against hers.
Aurelia found herself caught between two extremes: the desperate need to weep for her lost honor and the overwhelming, primal need to scream from the pleasure he forced upon her.
"Aaaahn! Rex... ahh... ahh!" Her voice rose in pitch as his fingers found sensitive places, sending sparks of lightning through her pelvis. "I hate you... mmm... ahh! I hate you so much!"
"Then hate me while you take this," he commanded, his voice rough with desire. "Hate me while you scream my name."
